venues.name: Jumeirah Burj Al Arab

venues.name: Atlantis The Royal

venues.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Dubai

venues.name: Mandarin Oriental Jumeira, Dubai

venues.name: Waldorf Astoria Dubai International Financial Centre

venues.name: Jumeirah Al Naseem

venues.name: The St. Regis Dubai, The Palm

venues.name: Address Beach Resort

venues.name: Grosvenor House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Dubai

venues.name: The Lana, Dorchester Collection

venues.name: One&Only Royal Mirage - The Residence

venues.name: Four Seasons Hotel Dubai International Financial Centre

venues.name: Jumeirah Al Qasr
venues.note: The grand 'palace' of the Madinat, with abras gliding to your door.

venues.name: Jumeirah Mina A'Salam

venues.name: Raffles The Palm Dubai
venues.note: Palatial, gilded and unabashedly grand, theatre with Raffles service.

venues.name: Anantara The Palm Dubai Resort

venues.name: Taj Dubai
venues.note: The house that speaks Hindi at the door and pours a proper chai.

venues.name: Palazzo Versace Dubai
venues.note: Full-throated Versace maximalism, Medusa on the marble and all.

venues.name: Atlantis The Palm
venues.note: The original Palm landmark, aquarium, waterpark, and dinner by Heston or Nobu.

venues.name: The Ritz-Carlton Dubai International Financial Centre
venues.note: A calm business-district Ritz-Carlton for meetings that end in the spa.

venues.name: Waldorf Astoria Dubai Palm Jumeirah

venues.name: Fairmont The Palm

venues.name: Sofitel Dubai The Palm

venues.name: Conrad Dubai
venues.note: A polished city tower on the main artery, reliable, central, unshowy.
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice 2024, No. 2 Hotel in Middle East (US)
World Travel Awards, Dubai's Leading Hotel 2024

venues.name: Kempinski Hotel Mall of the Emirates

venues.name: Banyan Tree Dubai

venues.name: Al Habtoor Palace, LXR Hotels & Resorts

venues.name: The St. Regis Downtown Dubai

venues.name: W Dubai - Mina Seyahi

venues.name: Address Downtown

venues.name: Address Sky View
venues.note: Twin towers joined by a sky bridge and a glass-floored infinity pool.

venues.name: Mandarin Oriental Downtown Dubai

venues.name: Palace Downtown

venues.name: Palace Dubai Creek Harbour

venues.note: A serene creek-side address away from the strip, looking to the flamingos.

venues.name: One&Only Royal Mirage - Arabian Court
venues.note: The family wing of the Royal Mirage, the same gardens, room for everyone.

venues.name: Le Royal Méridien Beach Resort & Spa
venues.note: An established beach resort with gardens that have had time to grow.

venues.name: Raffles The Palm, residences

venues.name: FIVE Palm Jumeirah
venues.note: The city's loudest pool party, for members who came to celebrate.

venues.name: JW Marriott Marquis Hotel Dubai
venues.note: Twin towers on the canal, big, capable, and easy on the wallet.

venues.name: Shangri-La Dubai
venues.note: A calm Asian-service tower on the main road, understated by Dubai standards.

venues.name: FZN by Björn Frantzén
venues.note: The Swedish master's Middle East debut, and one of only two three-stars in the city.

venues.name: Trèsind Studio

venues.name: STAY by Yannick Alléno
venues.note: Grand French dining, dessert library and all, in a garden setting.

venues.name: Row on 45
venues.note: A high, intimate counter where French technique meets Japanese omakase.

venues.name: Ossiano
venues.note: Dinner beside the aquarium wall, theatre that happens to be very good.

venues.name: Moonrise
venues.note: A rooftop counter for eight, the hardest, and warmest, seat in town.

venues.name: Dinner by Heston Blumenthal
venues.note: Heston's history-of-British-food, restaged with a Dubai view.

venues.name: Jun's
venues.note: Chef Kelvin Cheung's memory-cooking, Asian-American, personal, packed.

venues.name: Al Muntaha
venues.note: French cooking 200 metres up, inside the sail.

venues.name: La Dame de Pic Dubai
venues.note: Anne-Sophie Pic's delicate, aromatic French, translated to Dubai.

venues.name: Smoked Room
venues.note: Dani García's fire-and-smoke counter, Spanish, primal, precise.

venues.name: Tasca by José Avillez
venues.note: Portugal's finest, brought seaside, bright, generous, sunlit.

venues.name: Hakkasan
venues.note: The Cantonese standard-bearer, still holding its star after all these years.

venues.name: Hoseki
venues.note: A nine-seat omakase in a jewel-box room, the quietest luxury in town.

venues.name: Avatāra
venues.note: A vegetarian Indian tasting menu that earned a star on its own terms.

venues.name: Jamavar
venues.note: The Leela's grand Indian house, newly starred in Dubai.

venues.name: Manāo
venues.note: A newly-starred Thai kitchen doing quiet, exacting regional cooking.

venues.name: 11 Woodfire
venues.note: Everything touched by fire, a chef's-counter ode to the flame.

venues.name: Zuma
venues.note: The izakaya that set the template for the whole city, still full every night.

venues.name: LPM Restaurant & Bar
venues.note: Riviera cooking and a room that has never gone out of fashion.

venues.name: Gaia
venues.note: Greek cooking with a designer's eye, as much scene as supper.
credentials: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants (No. 35, 2024), DIFC's dressed-up late room

venues.name: Boca

venues.name: Mimi Kakushi
venues.note: 1920s-Osaka glamour and Japanese cooking with real intent.
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 36), Best Bar in the Middle East

venues.name: Bait Maryam
venues.note: A Levantine home kitchen, run like family, because it is.

venues.name: Lowe
venues.note: Zero-waste, market-led cooking with a conscience and a sense of humour.

venues.name: 3Fils
venues.note: A tiny harbour-side counter that outranks half the city's grand rooms.

venues.name: Kinoya
venues.note: Soulful Japanese comfort food, ramen and izakaya done properly.

venues.name: 21 Grams
venues.note: Balkan home cooking with heart, the antidote to Dubai gloss.

venues.name: Indya by Vineet
venues.note: Vineet Bhatia's contemporary Indian, at a price that flatters the cooking.

venues.name: Berenjak
venues.note: Tehran's back-street kebab houses, recreated with real fire and flatbread.

venues.name: Shabestan
venues.note: Old-Dubai Persian dining on the creek, saffron and all.

venues.name: Teible
venues.note: Farm-to-table restraint in a design-museum setting.

venues.name: Konjiki Hototogisu
venues.note: A Tokyo ramen name that earned its Bib on the bowl alone.

venues.name: Hoe Lee Kow
venues.note: Unfussy Asian comfort food with a devoted local following.

venues.name: Al Khayma Heritage Restaurant
venues.note: Emirati home cooking in a wind-tower courtyard house, the real old Dubai.

venues.name: Goldfish
venues.note: Sushi and seafood done cleanly and without fuss, a neighbourhood gem.

venues.name: Aamara
venues.note: Indian cooking with a light, modern hand, Bib-listed and easy to love.

venues.name: Revelry
venues.note: A gastro-room that punches above its price, Bib-approved.

venues.name: Hawkerboi
venues.note: Southeast-Asian hawker flavours with real fire and swagger.

venues.name: Khadak
venues.note: Indian street-food energy, credentialed by the Michelin inspectors.

venues.name: Sufret Maryam
venues.note: Bait Maryam's sister, the same Levantine warmth, a lighter setting.

venues.name: Harummanis
venues.note: Malaysian home cooking, gently spiced, quietly excellent.

venues.name: DUO Gastrobar
venues.note: A neighbourhood gastrobar that keeps earning its Bib across outlets.

venues.name: Bombay Brasserie
venues.note: Grand Indian dining under the Taj's own roof, nostalgic and assured.

venues.name: Bombay Bungalow
venues.note: Beach-side Indian street food and curries, bright, fresh, unpretentious.

venues.name: Burj Khalifa, At the Top
venues.note: The world's tallest building at 828m. Ride to the Level 124/125 deck, or book the quieter, pricier At the Top SKY (148) or a private table at The Lounge on 152-154 for canapés and champagne well above the crowds. Time it for late afternoon so you catch the city in daylight and then lit up at dusk.
credentials: Guinness World Record, tallest building in the world

venues.name: The Dubai Fountain
venues.note: The choreographed fountain on Burj Lake shoots water up to 150m to Arabic and world music, on the half-hour every evening. Free to watch from the Waterfront promenade; for a calmer view, book a lakeside table at a Souk Al Bahar restaurant or a short abra ride across the lake.

venues.name: The Dubai Mall
venues.note: One of the world's largest and most-visited malls, and the anchor of Downtown. Beyond 1,200 stores it holds the aquarium, an Olympic-size ice rink, and the fashion-avenue luxury wing. A practical base for a multi-generation family: air-conditioned, endless dining including plentiful Indian and vegetarian options, and direct access to the Burj and fountain.

venues.name: Museum of the Future
venues.note: The torus-shaped building wrapped in Arabic calligraphy is a landmark in its own right, and inside it is Dubai's most imaginative attraction, immersive, theatrical exhibits on space, ecology and wellbeing. Book a timed slot well ahead; it sells out. Genuinely engaging for teenagers and curious adults.

venues.name: Old Dubai by abra across the Creek
venues.note: Cross Dubai Creek on a wooden abra for a single dirham, the oldest, most atmospheric way to move through the city. It links the Deira souks with Bur Dubai's heritage quarter, and shows you the trading port the whole city grew from. Do it early morning or golden hour.

venues.name: Gold Souk
venues.note: Hundreds of shops in covered lanes with windows stacked in gold, one of the largest gold markets in the world, and a rite of passage for Indian visitors who know their carat and their making-charges. Prices track the daily rate, so bargain hard on the workmanship. Best in the cooler evening.

venues.name: Spice Souk
venues.note: A short walk from the Gold Souk, narrow alleys heaped with saffron, dried limes, frankincense, cardamom and chillies. More about the smell and colour than serious shopping, though the saffron and oud are worth buying. Pairs naturally with the abra and the gold market for a half-day in old Deira.

venues.name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
venues.note: Dubai's best-preserved old quarter, coral-and-gypsum houses, wind-tower coolers and quiet sikkas (lanes) from the late 1800s. Wander the galleries, the Coffee Museum, and courtyard cafés, then join the cultural centre's guided walk. A rare slow, shaded corner of the city.

venues.name: Al Shindagha Museum
venues.note: The UAE's largest heritage museum, a stretch of restored waterfront houses telling the story of the Creek, pearling, perfume and the ruling family, with modern interactive displays. More substantial and better curated than the old Dubai Museum, and an easy, cool, family-friendly cultural afternoon.

venues.name: Atlantis Aquaventure & The Lost Chambers
venues.note: One of the world's largest waterparks, with record-height slides, a shark-and-ray lagoon and a private beach, plus the adjoining Lost Chambers aquarium of 65,000 marine animals. The standout family day on the Palm; stay at Atlantis The Palm or Atlantis The Royal for direct access and skip-the-queue ease.

venues.name: The View at The Palm
venues.note: An observation deck 240m up in the Palm Tower, giving the one photo everyone wants, the whole palm-shaped island laid out below with the sea and skyline beyond. Quieter and cheaper than the Burj Khalifa deck, and the best place to actually grasp the scale of the Palm. Book a sunset slot.

venues.name: Burj Al Arab afternoon tea or dinner
venues.note: The sail-shaped hotel is off-limits unless you have a reservation, so book afternoon tea in the atrium's Sahn Eddar or a table at the Skyview Bar to actually get inside the icon. The gold-leaf interiors are deliberately over the top; go for the experience and the view, not restraint.

venues.name: Platinum Heritage luxury desert safari
venues.note: The discerning way to do the desert, vintage 1950s Land Rovers in a protected reserve, falconry, camel treks and a private Bedouin-camp dinner, run by one of the few licensed conservation operators. Choose a private vehicle to skip the dune-bashing party crowds; excellent for families and multi-gen groups.

venues.name: Jumeirah Mosque
venues.note: One of the few Dubai mosques open to non-Muslims, via the Sheikh Mohammed Centre's 'Open Doors, Open Minds' guided tours where you can ask anything over Emirati coffee and dates. The most approachable window into local faith and custom, and beautifully lit at night from the outside.

venues.name: Alserkal Avenue
venues.note: A warehouse district turned contemporary-art hub, Dubai's serious galleries, artist studios, indie cinema, specialty coffee and concept stores, all in raw industrial units. Where the city's real creative scene lives, far from the malls. Check what's showing before you go; openings are the moment.

venues.name: Jameel Arts Centre
venues.note: A calm, well-funded contemporary-art museum on the Creek with rotating exhibitions, an art library, sculpture gardens and a rooftop. Free entry, rarely crowded, and a thoughtful counterpoint to Dubai's louder attractions. A good rainy-heat-of-day cultural stop.

venues.name: Etihad Museum
venues.note: Built on the spot where the UAE was founded in 1971, an elegant modern museum telling the story of unification through the original documents, films and the founding fathers. Compact, well-designed and the clearest explanation of how this country came to be.

venues.name: Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary
venues.note: A protected wetland minutes from Downtown where thousands of pink flamingos wade against a backdrop of skyscrapers. Free hides with binoculars look out over the lagoon; best in the cool winter months when migratory birds arrive. A surprising, peaceful hour for families and photographers.

venues.name: Dubai Frame
venues.note: A 150m golden picture-frame you ride to the top of, with a glass-floor skywalk and Old Dubai on one side, New Dubai on the other, the city's past-and-future divide made literal. Quick, cheap and photogenic; set inside Zabeel Park for a walk afterward.

venues.name: Dubai Miracle Garden
venues.note: The world's largest natural flower garden, over 150 million blooms shaped into arches, hearts and a flower-covered Emirates A380. Open only in the cool season (roughly November to May) and heaving with families; go on a weekday morning. Pure spectacle, and a hit with children.
credentials: Guinness World Record, largest vertical garden

venues.name: Global Village
venues.note: A seasonal cultural theme park where 90-plus countries set up pavilions of crafts, street food and shows, a lively bazaar-meets-carnival. Open winter only. Chaotic and fun for families and groups; a low-cost, high-energy evening with a strong South-Asian food presence.

venues.name: Ski Dubai
venues.note: A full indoor snow resort inside a mall, real snow, ski and toboggan runs, and a colony of king and gentoo penguins you can meet. Absurd, and exactly why it delights children in the desert heat. Book the penguin encounter separately if that's the draw.

venues.name: The Green Planet
venues.note: An indoor tropical rainforest under a glass biodome, one of the region's largest indoor trees, sloths, snakes and free-flying birds across four humid levels. Compact, cool and hands-on; an easy 90 minutes that younger children love.

venues.name: Al Seef
venues.note: A 1.8km stretch of Creek-front rebuilt in old-Dubai style, wind towers, sandstone lanes, floating market, cafés and abra stations, that flows straight into the historic quarter. A pleasant, walkable evening by the water with dhows drifting past. Family-friendly and easy.

venues.name: Kite Beach
venues.note: The best free public beach for activity, kitesurfing, paddleboarding, a running track and casual beach cafés, all with a clean sweep of Burj Al Arab views. More energetic and local than the resort strips; good for an active family morning before the heat.

venues.name: J1 Beach
venues.note: The Riviera-style beach-club strip that replaced La Mer, 13 upscale dining and beach-club concepts arriving from St-Tropez, Cannes and Tulum along a 500m shoreline. Book a daybed at one of the clubs for a polished, licensed beach day. The current centre of gravity for Dubai's beach scene.

venues.name: Dubai Marina & JBR walk
venues.note: Stroll the Marina promenade past superyachts and glass towers, then the buzzing beachfront of The Walk at JBR, full of cafés, street performers and people-watching. The most Miami-like part of the city; lovely in the evening. Add a short yacht or dhow cruise from the Marina to see it from the water.

venues.name: Sunset yacht or dhow cruise from the Marina
venues.note: Charter a private yacht (or join a smaller shared cruise) out past the Marina towers, Bluewaters, JBR and the Palm crescent as the skyline lights up. The private charter is the discreet, family-friendly choice, your own deck, catering and swim stop, away from the party boats.

venues.name: Bluewaters Island & Ain Dubai
venues.note: A polished dining-and-leisure island connected to JBR, dominated by Ain Dubai, the world's tallest observation wheel at 250m, a striking skyline landmark even when ride operations are paused, so check its status before counting on a spin. Come for the waterfront restaurants and the view of it either way.
credentials: Guinness World Record, tallest observation wheel (Ain Dubai)

venues.name: Coffee Museum
venues.note: A small, characterful museum in a heritage house tracing coffee across cultures, with antique roasters and a majlis serving traditional Emirati gahwa. A charming, quiet stop while wandering Al Fahidi, the kind of hidden gem that rewards the curious.

venues.name: XVA Gallery
venues.note: A leading contemporary gallery of Arab and Iranian art tucked into a courtyard heritage house, with a shaded vegetarian café and a tiny boutique hotel. An unhurried, cultured pause in the old town, art, mint lemonade and wind-tower shade.

venues.name: Textile Souk
venues.note: The covered fabric market on the Bur Dubai side of the Creek, bolts of silk, pashmina and embroidered cloth, and the landing point for the abra from Deira. Bring your bargaining; it's a lively, old-world stretch that pairs with Al Fahidi next door.

venues.name: Al Qudra Lakes & Love Lake
venues.note: Man-made desert lakes on the edge of the city, a cycling and picnic spot where you'll spot swans, oryx and migratory birds, plus the two intertwined heart-shaped Love Lakes. Cool, quiet and best at dawn or dusk; bring a car and your own supplies.

venues.name: Deep Dive Dubai
venues.note: The world's deepest swimming pool at 60m, built as a sunken city you dive or freedive through, with an underwater restaurant window. A genuinely unusual, bookable experience for divers and confident swimmers; sessions are limited, so reserve ahead.
credentials: Guinness World Record, deepest swimming pool for diving

venues.name: Dubai Opera
venues.note: A dhow-shaped venue at the foot of the Burj Khalifa staging opera, ballet, orchestras, musicals and big-name concerts. The most refined night out in the city, and a rare chance to dress up; check the season's programme and book a box for the fountain-side arrival.

venues.name: La Perle by Dragone
venues.note: Dubai's resident aqua-theatre spectacular, acrobatics, high dives and stunts in a purpose-built theatre with a stage that floods with water. Slick, wordless and family-friendly; the closest thing to a Cirque-style show in the city. Book weekend seats early.

venues.name: City Walk & Coca-Cola Arena
venues.note: A low-rise, European-style dining-and-shopping district that's pleasant to stroll on cooler evenings, anchored by the region's largest indoor arena for concerts and comedy. A relaxed alternative to the mega-malls, with wide pavements and good restaurants for families.

venues.name: Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo
venues.note: One of the world's largest suspended aquarium tanks, viewable free from the mall or up close via the walk-through tunnel, glass-bottom boat and cage-snorkelling. An easy, reliable crowd-pleaser for children when you need an air-conditioned hour inside The Dubai Mall.

venues.name: Skydive Dubai, Palm drop zone
venues.note: A tandem jump over the Palm, freefalling with the whole island and coastline unfurling beneath you, arguably the most spectacular urban skydive on earth. No experience needed; book weeks ahead as slots go fast. The bucket-list thrill for adventurous visitors.

venues.name: Mall of the Emirates & indoor entertainment
venues.note: Beyond Ski Dubai, this is a genuinely upscale mall with a strong luxury wing, a cinema and VOX gold-class screens, and Magic Planet for kids. A cool-weather-independent day when the heat is punishing, with plentiful vegetarian and Indian dining nearby.

venues.name: Palm Jumeirah Boardwalk & The Pointe
venues.note: An 11km promenade along the Palm's crescent for a sea-air walk with Atlantis and the skyline in view, ending at waterfront dining. A calmer, free way to experience the Palm on foot, best at sunset when the light is soft and the heat lifts.

venues.name: Mimi Kakushi
venues.note: 1920s Osaka glamour and serious mixology, the most decorated bar in the region, and it shows.
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 36), Best Bar in the Middle East

venues.name: Galaxy Bar
venues.note: An intimate, constellation-lit room in the financial district, cocktails made with real intent.

venues.name: La Petite Maison (LPM), bar
venues.note: The Riviera room the city never tires of, a pre-dinner drink here is a Dubai ritual.

venues.name: Skyview Bar, Burj Al Arab
venues.note: A drink 200 metres up inside the sail, the view most first visits are chasing.
credentials: Inside Burj Al Arab, global landmark venue

venues.name: Gold on 27, Burj Al Arab
venues.note: A gilded, theatrical cocktail room high in the sail, indulgence taken entirely seriously.
credentials: Inside Burj Al Arab, signature high-concept cocktail bar

venues.name: CÉ LA VI Dubai
venues.note: The Burj Khalifa filling the glass, 54 floors up, the rooftop that best frames Downtown.
credentials: Internationally recognised rooftop group, Address Sky View, 54th floor

venues.name: Above Eleven
venues.note: A neon-lit rooftop with Peruvian-Japanese plates and skyline views, Bangkok's cult name, restaged.
credentials: World Luxury Restaurant Awards, recognised rooftop; established international name

venues.name: Zuma bar
venues.note: The bar that set the template for grown-up Dubai nights, still full, still faultless.
credentials: Zuma, MENA's 50 Best Restaurants; the district's benchmark bar-and-dining room

venues.name: Gaia
venues.note: Greek glamour and a dressed-up crowd, as much a scene as a supper, well past midnight.
credentials: MENA's 50 Best Restaurants (No. 35, 2024), DIFC's dressed-up late room
